thread.title: Morning Brief: U.S.-China trade talks to resume

author: Yahoo Finance
title: Morning Brief: U.S.-China trade talks to resume
text:
morning brief More Thursday, December 27, 2018
Get the Morning Brief sent directly to your inbox every Monday to Friday by 6:30 a.m. ET. Subscribe
WHAT TO WATCH
The Dow and S&P 500 each booked their biggest one-day point gains in history . Is this the beginning of a recovery in the markets? Or is it just a dead cat bounce? We’ll see.
Due to the partial government shutdown, monthly new home sales data that was scheduled to be released Thursday morning has been postponed indefinitely. However, the U.S. Department of Labor’s report on initial jobless claims for the week ending December 22 and continuing claims for the week ending December 15 will be released as usual. Economist polled by Bloomberg are expecting initial jobless claims to have risen to a seasonally-adjusted 216,000 units.
Read more
TOP NEWS
FILE - In this Sept. 16, 2018, file photo, American flags are displayed together with Chinese flags on top of a trishaw in Beijing. China’s Commerce Ministry said Thursday, Nov. 15, 2018, that high-level trade talks between Washington and Beijing have resumed. (AP Photo/Andy Wong, File) More US-China trade talks to take place in Beijing in early January : A U.S. government delegation will travel to Beijing in the week of Jan. 7 to hold trade talks with Chinese officials, two people familiar with the matter said. [Bloomberg]
White House considers new year exec order to bar Huawei, ZTE purchases : President Donald Trump is considering an executive order in the new year to declare a national emergency that would bar U.S. companies from using telecommunications equipment made by China's Huawei and ZTE, three sources familiar with the situation told Reuters. [Reuters]
China’s JD.com plans $1B share buyback : Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com ( JD ) announced a $1 billion share buyback program in a bid to lift stock prices weighed down by concerns about China’s economy and potential sexual-assault charges against the company’s chief executive. [The Wall Street Journal]
JPMorgan to pay $135 million for improper handling of ADRs : JPMorgan Chase & Co. ( JPM ) will pay $135 million to settle Securities and Exchange Commission allegations that it mishandled U.S. securities that represent shares of foreign companies, the latest bank fined in an industry crackdown on the practice. [Bloomberg]
Foxconn to assemble top-end Apple iPhones in India : Apple Inc ( AAPL ) will begin assembling its top-end iPhones in India through the local unit of Foxconn as early as 2019, the first time the Taiwanese contract manufacturer will have made the product in the country, according to a source familiar with the matter. [Reuters]
